sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The window is a steady compounding rather than a step change, with the two inflection years FY2021 and FY2022 lifting growth to 17.5% and 15.8% [D189][D238].
FY2021's 17.5% revenue growth came from a 16% comparable sales increase, strong non-foods and e-commerce, plus gasoline and currency tailwinds [D189][P56][P55].
FY2022's 15.8% growth was driven by a 14% comparable sales increase and inflation, with gasoline, business centers and travel strongest [D238][P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of its 10.1% growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp [D670][D672][D679][D434].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, 10%, on an 8% comparable sales increase from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of FY2026 revenue but contributed only 2.6pp of growth, while warehouse ancillary added 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Operating income grew 12.3% a year against 10.0% for revenue, and FY2026 incremental operating margin was 4.7% [F204][F203][D457].
Operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026, with SG&A growth at 8.9% [D458][D450].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, above the 3.4% window median and at the window high, against a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D692][D691][D690].
The FY2026 bridge was flat on cost of revenue and plus 0.1pp on SG&A, for a 0.1pp gain [D459][D460][D447].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with currency adding $126 million [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.8pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap the pack puts at -0.8pp [F52][F32][D732].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, above the 1.75x window median [F82][F42][D421][D722].
The increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income and a 3.1% margin, above the 2.8% window median [F102][F42][D422][D418][D698].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F92][F10][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, 5.0% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of four retail peers against a -18.3% median [D427][D428][D733][D734].
Total debt of $6.2 billion includes $2.2 billion current, and long-term debt fell 31.5% in FY2026 [D426][X160][D445].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, and repurchases of $847 million retired 891,000 shares [D429][D430][P3].
The diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million, so EPS growth of 14.0% tracked net income growth of 13.9% [X100][D438][D436].
Operating margin of 3.9% sits in the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin of 3.0% is also 17th against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].
The thin margin is structural to the membership model rather than a deterioration, since the margin has risen from 3.2% in FY2017 to 3.9% [F23][F32].
Capex has grown 11.1% a year against 10.0% for revenue, lifting capex to 2.41x D&A from 1.83x in FY2017 [F209][F203][D423][D11].
Rising capital intensity is the main watch point, since free cash flow margin of 3.1% still trails the 3.6% window high [D418][D697].
Whether operating margin holds at or above the 3.9% FY2026 level or slips toward the 3.4% window median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D692].
Whether free cash flow per net income stays at or above the 0.99x window median from 1.02x in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D701][D422].
Whether capex to D&A falls back toward the 2.27x FY2025 level from 2.41x, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D374][D423].
